correctness.rationale: All parameters and boundaries are explicit. Product Haar yields independent Voronoi increments; closing edge is the negative Voronoi representative, giving \(W=S-R\). Symmetric convolution gives the exact lattice law. For \(m\ge3\), R is independent of each increment, yielding exact covariance \(m\Sigma\). A compact full-dimensional even density has L2 characteristic function and positive covariance, so Fourier inversion with a fourth-order Taylor remainder gives the uniform \(O_L(m^{-d/2-1})\) local limit. Direct rational Eulerian checks \(3\le m\le13\) and 690000 separately generated direct-geodesic polygon samples corroborate the algebra and hex/square geometric covariances; finite checks are not relied upon as proofs. The hex polar-area moment was also independently recomputed by polygon integration.

value.rationale: A natural geometric-probability question asks for the full homotopy class of a shortest-geodesic polygon with Haar random vertices. The all-length vector distribution, exact finite-length covariance as a Voronoi moment, and the persistent square/hexagonal leading ratio resolve structural aspects not supplied by a single triangle probability or an Eulerian coefficient table. The finite-sample invariants and shape effect have plausible use in distinguishing and modeling geodesic-loop homology; no claim of global extremality, stability or a broader new CLT is needed.
